can_answer: yes, for the distribution of recorded crash rows across weekdays in the requested years; not a population-adjusted crash risk comparison
metric: Number of police-reported crash rows by weekday, pooled across 2013–2025
denominator: Count of crash rows (no rate denominator)
population: All crash rows whose crash_date falls from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31
grouping: Day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
limitations: Counts describe police-reported crash rows, not crash rates per day of exposure or traffic volume. All 13 requested years have complete calendar coverage; the date field is DATE-typed with 0 missing values across the source and therefore no invalid weekday derivations. The final population includes all 2,132,218 dated crash rows from 2013–2025 without exclusions. Annual row counts vary substantially: the largest neighboring-year change is a decrease of 98,568 rows, from 211,486 in 2019 to 112,918 in 2020, so pooled weekday counts combine years with different numbers of crash records.

data_check.decision: Keep all dated records and disclose the record-count variation; no rows are dropped or treated as a separate group. crash_date missing in source: 0; impossible values: 0 possible in a DATE-typed column; all requested years have full Jan 1–Dec 31 coverage. There are 2,132,218 rows in the final population.
data_check.final_population: All crash rows with crash_date from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31; 2,132,218 rows, no date-based exclusions.
